An escrow is a shared wallet. Several people each hold one key, and you choose how many of them must approve a payment, for example 2 of 3 with buyer, seller and a neutral person. Nobody can spend alone unless you choose 1.

This app runs a full copy of the Elektron network on your phone. It checks every payment itself instead of trusting a server. It syncs in the background and uses some data and battery. You decide when it runs and you can pause or stop it at any time.
The first sync downloads a lot of data. Wi-Fi only is recommended. You can change this later in Settings.
The node runs in the background and shows its status in a notification. You can pause or stop it there.

Add my own randomness by drawing

Move your finger around the box in an irregular way until the bar is full. Your movements are mixed into the random numbers of the phone as extra protection. Straight lines, tiny movements and repeated patterns do not count.
Roll a normal six-sided die at least %1$d times and type each result, digits 1 to 6. Use a real die and shake it well. Do not make up numbers.

The words come from your dice alone. You can recompute them yourself with SHA-256 of the digits. Only safe if every roll is real.

Asks a price service for the ELEK rate. The service sees your IP address. Off: only ELEK is shown.
Address (https), {BASE} and {QUOTE} are replaced by the pair
Path to the price in the answer

Example: https://api.example.org/ticker/{BASE}-{QUOTE} with the path data.price. {base} and {quote} are the lowercase forms, both also work in the path. Numbers pick a list entry (data.0.last), * takes the first entry of an object. To test without a real market, use a fixed address: https://api.coingecko.com/api/v3/simple/price?ids=bitcoin&vs_currencies={quote} with the path bitcoin.{quote}. The result then stands in for the ELEK price.

Spend coins on reused addresses automatically

On (default): coins on reused addresses count as available and are added when the other coins do not cover a payment, also when you send everything. Off: they are not counted and never mixed with other coins, and a payment that fits into one reused address is still paid from it first. Switch it off if you do not want to link such addresses.
Switch it off if your network has no IPv6. The I2P router then stops trying IPv6 and the \"Network is unreachable\" lines disappear from the log.

Escrows of wallet %1$s. Every wallet has its own escrows.
How many keys must approve a payment
With 1 key, every key holder can spend alone. This is not an escrow protection.

This creates your own key for the deal. You choose the number of approvals later, in step 2, after you added the keys of the others. The passphrase of this wallet unlocks the key once. The key line you get cannot be used to spend.

How an escrow works:
1. Everyone in the deal creates an escrow here and gets a key line.
2. Everyone sends the key line to the others and adds the lines of the others.
3. Everyone chooses the same number of approvals, for example 2 of 3, and creates the escrow wallet. Nothing has to be decided before this step.
4. Compare the check code and the deposit address. They must be identical for everyone.
5. Send coins to the deposit address. To pay, one person creates a payment, the others sign it until enough approvals are there.
Applies to the logs of the node, Tor and I2P. Older lines and everything above the size are removed about once an hour. Wallet files are never touched.

Groups long numbers, for example 1,234,567.89. The default follows your language and country.
The default for your language and country is %1$s. You can choose other characters.

\"Deposit from my wallet\" sends coins from your own wallet into the escrow. \"Pay out of the escrow\" spends the coins that are already in the escrow: it creates a payment request that needs the approvals of the other people.

You are paying out of the escrow, not out of your own wallet. The available amount is the balance of the escrow. This creates a payment request that the others must approve. To put coins into the escrow, use \"Deposit from my wallet\" on the escrow page.
